- Exercises policy-as-code and CI integration

- Kyverno policy, Kubernetes securityContext, multi-resource kinds, CI gates

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-container-hardening
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-container-security
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, privileged: false; pod runAsNonRoot: true"

          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: "*"

                  privileged: false
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a scalable, automated policy gate across multi-cloud clusters using Gatekeeper/OPA, Cosign attestations, and runtime security constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Cosign attestation and image provenance
- Registry allowlist and image provenance checks
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop capabilities
- CI integration and gatekeeper audit verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (Gatekeeper) minimal sketch
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecuredcontainers
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecuredContainers
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8ssecuredcontainers
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not signed(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Container image %v must be cosign-signed", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not allowed_registry(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Registry %v not in allowlist", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
          msg := "Container must run as non-root"
        }
```

## What to Look For

- Demonstrates understanding of OPA/Gatekeeper policy structure
- Shows proper cosign attestation validation approach
- Includes comprehensive runtime security constraints
- Outlines practical CI/CD integration strategy

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable, enforceable policy gates across clouds with image provenance and hardening.

## Key Concepts
- Image provenance (Sigstore Cosign)
- SecurityContext: RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.drop ALL
- RBAC: namespace scoping and least privilege
- Policy engines: Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- CI verification: cosign verify, dry-run manifests, local validation

## Code Example
```javascript
name: CI Gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify image signatures
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ env.IMAGE }}
      - name: Validate manifests (dry-run)
        run: kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f k8s/
```

```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "containers must set RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
```

## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation
